summary: Well-executed, well-documented preregistered emulation study that transparently archives artifacts and shows a null confirmatory result driven by preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics. The experiment and analysis appear reproducible and internally consistent, but the manuscript must more clearly acknowledge and explain that the preregistered primary estimand became untestable because baseline performance was 100%, and must report a small set of operational summary facts more explicitly.
critical_issues: The primary confirmatory estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) is effectively untestable given the observed ceiling (baseline_success_rate = 100%). The manuscript does not state explicitly enough that the preregistered hypothesis could not be meaningfully evaluated because there were no discordant pairs; this must be made explicit in the abstract, methods (analysis/power discussion), results, and limitations.

The manuscript should explicitly report the number of repair attempts invoked (and/or repair calls actually executed) and explain concisely that zero repairs were applied so the guarded pipeline was never exercised; while implied, this factual count is essential and must be stated plainly in Results and the Disclosure Statement.
required_revisions: Add explicit, unambiguous language that the preregistered primary estimand became uninformative/untestable because baseline performance was 100% (complete ceiling effect) and explain consequences for statistical inference and for the preregistered power assumptions (which had assumed baseline 30%–60%). Place this statement in the Abstract, Methods (power/analysis subsection), Results, and Limitations.

Add an explicit summary count of repair-stage activity (e.g., "repair calls invoked: 0; repair_applied_count: 0") and a short sentence in Results stating that the guarded repair stage was never invoked for any pair and therefore could not provide benefit in this run. Also clarify the model-call accounting (model_calls_used=200) as a direct consequence of shared_initial_candidate semantics in the Methods/Execution-accounting text.
optional_revisions: Consider softening the title slightly to emphasize the design-bound scope (e.g., include "under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics") to reduce risk of misinterpretation by readers skimming titles.
Expand Related Work to cite and briefly contrast any recent studies that used independent-condition generation or iterative repair budgets, to better position the diagnostic lessons offered here.

Add one short paragraph in Discussion proposing precise follow-up preregistered designs (independent generation, larger repair budget, or targeted higher-difficulty tasks) and, if feasible, provide a small worked example from the artifact bundle illustrating a hypothetical discordant case (if any exist in development logs) — only as illustrative text, not new experiments.
